title: Support for Point-to-Point Sector Given Rising Petrol Prices and Slow Recovery in Passenger Numbers
what_it_is: Support for Point-to-Point Sector Given Rising Petrol Prices and Slow Recovery in Passenger Numbers

sections.label: P2P driver support measures
sections.summary: The Government set aside over $1 billion for P2P driver support, including PPSP, SIRS, CDRF, road tax and petrol duty rebates, and has no plans for more fuel cost support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Amid lower ridership, the Government has set aside more than $1 billion to provide broad-based as well as sector-specific support to the P2P drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Since February 2020, the Government has introduced the Point-to-Point Support Package (PPSP), Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) and multiple tranches of COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund (CDRF).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To mitigate the financial impact of this on active P2P drivers with petrol vehicles, the Government provided road tax rebate of 15%, which is about $120, as well as additional petrol duty rebate of $360 in 2021 as offsets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: P2P ridership has steadily recovered from about 70% of pre-COVID-19 levels in October 2021 during the Stabilisation Period, to about 80% in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Government currently has no plans to provide additional support to defray higher fuel costs which is the result of market forces of global supply and demand factors.

sections.label: Taxi fare deregulation 1998
sections.summary: For taxis, fares were deregulated in 1998.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, for taxis, in 1998, we had deregulated the fares.

sections.label: P2P fare notice and multi-homing
sections.summary: The Government does not regulate fares but requires operators to give the Public Transport Council advance notice of fare adjustments, and the P2P framework lets taxi drivers multi-home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: What the Government does – it does not regulate fares – is that it requires the operators to provide the Public Transport Council advance notice of any fare adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Additionally, what we have also done is to ensure that the P2P regulatory framework provides an open P2P market so that the taxi drivers are allowed to multi-home, instead of just driving exclusively for one operator.
